note:
staging takes 1.5.0. One release is crossed, 1.4.5 to 1.5.0, and nothing is
skipped, so no skipped release carries a landing section anybody has to read.

The releases: class fix and feature, disruption quiet. No core floor moves.
Codex stays at 0.147.0 and Claude stays at 2.1.227, the same values 1.4.5
declared.

The box, measured on staging at 10:54Z before this note was written:
claw-members holds one person. That person's persistent core is installed and
reads 2.1.227, and their per-task core reads 0.147.0. Both meet the floors this
release declares, so no member reads as below one and this claw's own classifier
will not defer the release to the quiet window.

The same reading for the thing this release adds: this claw has no email-gate
account, no mail service, nothing under /srv/connections, and no provider key.
That is the state every claw is in when this release lands.

This release installs a mail service under its own system account, email-gate,
and no claw carries a provider key for it. A firm puts that key into its own
machine vault with install-email-provider-key.sh and makes the address once with
email inbox create. Until the key is there the service reaches no provider, and
the apply says so twice in notes that name both doors.

A firm's email orchestrator is a separate thing and it does not arrive here. It
is launched from the email skill in the open library, which writes the firm's
communication runbook and then records where it put it with
email self set runbook. This payload carries no skill: the fleet manifest
declares claw-ops alone and the assembler names claw-ops alone.

An update run by hand no longer reports every other member's git identity as
missing. The people phase reached each member from wherever the operator was
standing, and one member cannot look inside another member's home, so the read
died there and the run said the identity was absent. From 1.5.0 those git calls
stand at the root of the filesystem. Ride from there.
